full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Delwar Hossain, J:- This Rule upon an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why 3621 days delay in preferring the appeal against the judgment and order dated 3.3.1999 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court, Kushtia in Sessions Case No.2 of 1997 convicting the appellant petitioner under section 302/34 of the Penal Code should not be condoned and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The appellant petitioner was convicted under section 302/34 of the Penal Code along with two others and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay fine of Tk. 5,000/- in default to suffer 6(six) months more. In the application for condonation of delay it has been stated that the petitioner was not aware of the case for the alleged occurrence of 2.9.1995. Due to heavy erosion of the river Padma the petitioner lost his residence at village Insaf Nagar, Police Station Daulatpur, District Kushtia in 1994 and left for Rajpara under Rajshahi district where he settled. When on 29.8.2008 he came to see his previous residence at village Insaf Nagar he was arrested by the police in connection with the said case and came to know for the first time that he was tried for the alleged occurrence and convicted and sentenced in his absence. He was produced before the Court of Magistrate on the following day and was sent to jail to suffer the sentence. Thereafter the tadbirkar of the petitioner collecting the certified copies of the judgment and order and other papers came to Dhaka and engaging the learned Advocate handed over those for preferring an appeal against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence. The learned Advocate preparing the petition of appeal filed the same on 15.3.2009 and thereby delay of 3621 days has been caused for which a separate application under section 5 of the Limitation Act has been filed for condonation of the said delay and obtained the Rule.
